title: Predicted climate shifts within terrestrial protected areas worldwide
problem: The effectiveness of static protected areas is threatened as climate change forces species to migrate, yet a fine-scale, global assessment of how climatic conditions will shift *within* these refugia is currently lacking, which hinders proactive conservation planning and adaptation.
method: To assess predicted climate shifts, we use Principal Component Analysis on bioclimatic data to define climate classes and then calculate the proportion of novel and disappearing climate conditions that are expected to occur within the world's terrestrial protected areas at local, regional, and global scales.
task: The task is to assess how climate conditions are expected to shift within the world's terrestrial protected areas by quantifying the future proportions of novel and disappearing climate conditions at local, regional, and global scales.
innovation: This paper presents a global, fine-resolution analysis quantifying future novel and disappearing climate conditions within 137,432 terrestrial protected areas, identifying temperate and high-latitude biomes as most vulnerable and providing a guide for targeted conservation adaptation measures.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Future climate data were downscaled from GCMs to the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 5 (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, Fifth Assessment Report). We implemented the Representative Concentration Pathway RCP 4.5 and 8.5, and the following global climate models (GCM) for the year 2070, i.e. the average of period 2061–2080: BCC-CSM1-1, CCSM4, CNRM-CM5, GFDL-CM3, HadGEM2-AO, INMCM4, IPSL-CM5A-LR, MIROC5, MPI-ESM-LR, and MRI-CGCM3.

kg_extraction_triplets.source_entity_instance: digital elevation model provided by Amatulli et al.45
kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: We extracted the median elevation of each PA from a digital elevation model with a resolution of 30 arc seconds provided by Amatulli et al.45.
This product is based on 90 m elevation data from the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission and has a final resolution of 30 arc seconds45.
